title: Lifecycle validation report
description: One harness run against one support row. Written by tools/validation/lifecycle-stages.sh and consumed by evidence-bundle assembly, which decides completeness from the stage set rather than from prose.

row_id.description: The support row this run validates. A report whose row is not in the registry is evidence for nothing.

subject.description: What was actually installed and exercised. A report that does not say what it tested cannot authorize a release: without it a run filed under one version silently blesses every later tag.

tested_version.description: The TensorPlate version installed on the machine under test, as the packages reported it. The release gate requires this to equal the version being released.

source_revision.description: Full git SHA of the source the tested artifacts were built from, when the harness can determine it.

artifact_digest.description: sha256 of the installed package, when the harness can determine it. Binds the report to one artifact rather than to a version string anyone can reuse.

harness.description: Which harness produced this run, for reproducing it.

outcome.description: pass only when all eight canonical stages are present and passed. fail when any stage failed. incomplete when nothing failed but the eight are not all present and passing -- a deliberate skip is not a breakage, and conflating the two would either hide a gap or invent a failure. Only pass satisfies the release gate.

stage.description: The eight lifecycle stages. A closed set so a report missing one is detectable rather than merely shorter.

started_at.description: When the stage began. Present only for a stage that ran.

finished_at.description: When the stage ended. Present only for a stage that ran.

log.description: Log file for this stage, relative to the report. Attached whether the stage passed or failed: a passing stage's log is what a later regression is diffed against.

detail.description: Why a stage failed or was skipped. Required for both, since an unexplained skip is indistinguishable from an omission.
